note: Composition and mechanical values are published standards data, reproduced for reference only. Always specify to the current revision of the governing standard.

grades.name: Inconel 625
grades.summary: A niobium-stabilised nickel-chromium-molybdenum alloy that gets its strength from solid-solution hardening rather than heat treatment, so it arrives strong and stays strong without post-weld ageing.
service: Resists pitting, crevice corrosion and chloride stress-corrosion cracking
Seawater and sour service, flue gas desulphurisation, chemical processing
Serviceable from cryogenic temperatures to roughly 980 °C

verify.risk: Niobium and molybdenum are the two most expensive elements in the alloy, so a price cut has to come out of one of them. Material light on Nb+Ta will still look like 625 on a certificate and still weld, and it will fail in service years early.
regime: PMI specified on the delivered heat, reading Nb+Ta and Mo against B443 limits
Certificate cross-checked to the heat number actually in the crate
EN 10204 3.1 or 3.2 as specified
Intergranular corrosion testing where the service calls for it

grades.tell: Niobium and molybdenum are the cost, so they are the thinning risk

grades.name: Inconel 718
grades.summary: A precipitation-hardening nickel-iron-chromium superalloy. Its properties come from a controlled solution and ageing cycle, which means the heat treatment matters as much as the chemistry.
service: High-strength service to roughly 700 °C
Downhole tooling, valves, turbine components, fasteners
Good weldability for a precipitation-hardened alloy — resists post-weld strain-age cracking

mechanical.value: Solution treated & aged, ASTM B637 — condition to be specified on order

verify.risk: 718 is the grade where chemistry alone proves nothing. An under-aged or incorrectly solution-treated heat has textbook composition and will not make its mechanical minimums. Certificates showing chemistry but vague heat-treatment records are the warning sign.
regime: Heat treatment records demanded and read, not just filed
Hardness and tensile verification on the delivered heat
PMI confirming Nb+Ta and Ti against B637
Grain size where the application is fatigue-driven

grades.tell: Chemistry proves nothing here; the heat treatment is the grade

grades.name: Hastelloy C-276
grades.summary: The reference nickel-molybdenum-chromium alloy for aggressive wet chemical service, and one of the few materials that handles both oxidising and reducing conditions without a change of grade.
service: Wet chlorine, hypochlorite, chlorine dioxide and ferric chloride
Sour gas, flue gas desulphurisation, pulp and paper bleaching
Very low carbon and silicon give excellent as-welded corrosion resistance

verify.risk: Molybdenum is the single most expensive element in the alloy, which puts the whole cost-down incentive on one number, and that number is invisible without measurement. Carbon is the second check: C-276's very low carbon ceiling is what gives it as-welded performance, and a heat over 0.010 % will sensitise at the weld.
regime: PMI specified on the delivered heat, reading Mo against the 15.0–17.0 window
Carbon verified against the 0.010 % maximum
ASTM G28 method A intergranular corrosion testing where specified
Solution anneal records confirmed

grades.tell: Molybdenum is the substitution tell on C-276

grades.name: Hastelloy C-22
grades.summary: A higher-chromium alternative to C-276 with better resistance to oxidising media and localised attack, and better as-welded stability across a wider range of conditions.
service: Oxidising and mixed acid service where C-276 is marginal
Pharmaceutical and chemical process vessels, scrubbers, flue gas systems
Outstanding resistance to pitting and crevice corrosion

verify.risk: C-22 and C-276 are easy to cross-sell in either direction: the two look identical in the crate, and their certificates read alike to anyone not checking the numbers. The alloys are not interchangeable: their chromium and molybdenum balance is different, and so is the service each one survives.
regime: PMI distinguishing Cr 20.0–22.5 and Mo 12.5–14.5 from the C-276 windows
Certificate matched to the heat number in the crate
ASTM G28 testing where specified
Confirmation the grade ordered is the grade quoted, in writing, before the PO

grades.tell: C-22 and C-276 are cross-sold in both directions

grades.name: Incoloy 825
grades.summary: A titanium-stabilised nickel-iron-chromium alloy with copper and molybdenum, engineered for both oxidising and reducing acids at a materially lower cost than the C-family alloys.
service: Sulphuric and phosphoric acid service, pickling plant, sour gas
Excellent resistance to chloride stress-corrosion cracking
Titanium stabilisation resists sensitisation after welding

verify.risk: 904L is cheaper, superficially similar and roughly half the nickel, which makes it the obvious substitution to attempt. The other failure is titanium below the 0.6 % floor, which removes the stabilisation that stops the alloy sensitising at the weld — a defect that only appears once the vessel is in service.
regime: PMI reading Ni against the 38.0–46.0 window to rule out a 904L substitution
Titanium verified against the 0.6 % minimum
Molybdenum and copper confirmed against B424
Stabilising anneal records where specified

grades.tell: A 904L substitution reads almost right until you measure nickel

grades.name: Incoloy 800H
grades.summary: The controlled-carbon, coarse-grain version of Incoloy 800, specified where creep and rupture strength at high temperature are the governing properties.
service: Sustained service above 600 °C — furnace tubing, heat treatment fixtures, petrochemical piping
Creep and stress-rupture strength well beyond standard 800
Resists carburisation and oxidation in cyclic heat

verify.risk: 800H is Incoloy 800 only if two things hold: carbon inside the narrow 0.05–0.10 % band, and grain size ASTM 5 or coarser after a high-temperature anneal. Standard 800 supplied against an 800H order will pass a chemistry-only check on most elements and then creep at temperature. This is the substitution that certificates hide best.
regime: Carbon verified against the 0.05–0.10 % band, not merely against a maximum
Grain size determination, which a chemistry-only certificate will not cover
Annealing temperature records demanded
PMI for Al+Ti against the 0.30–1.20 % window

grades.tell: 800H is 800 only if carbon and grain size both hold

grades.name: Monel 400
grades.summary: A solid-solution nickel-copper alloy, essentially unchanged in composition for over a century, and still the default for seawater and hydrofluoric acid service.
service: Seawater, brackish water and marine service — resists erosion and cavitation
Hydrofluoric acid, alkalis, and reducing conditions
Retains strength and toughness down to cryogenic temperatures

verify.risk: Nickel is roughly four times the price of copper, so the economic incentive runs one way: push nickel toward the 63 % floor and copper toward the 34 % ceiling. A heat sitting outside the ratio still looks like Monel and still machines like Monel, and it corrodes faster in exactly the seawater service it was bought for.
regime: PMI specified on the delivered heat, reading the Ni:Cu ratio rather than nickel alone
Iron verified against the 2.5 % maximum
Sulphur checked where hot working or welding is planned
Certificate matched to the heat number in the crate

grades.tell: Nickel costs four times copper, and the ratio is the alloy

grades.name: Super duplex 2507
grades.summary: A 25-chromium super duplex stainless with roughly double the yield strength of 316L, which usually means thinner sections and less weight for the same duty.
service: Seawater systems, desalination, offshore process piping
Chloride-bearing service where austenitic grades crack
PREN typically 42 or above

verify.risk: Duplex grades fail on structure, not chemistry. Incorrect solution annealing or an uncontrolled cool leaves intermetallic sigma phase and a ferrite balance outside 35–55 %, which destroys toughness and corrosion resistance while every element on the certificate still reads in range. Nitrogen at the low end also quietly drops the PREN below what was specified.
regime: Ferrite content measured on the delivered material
PREN calculated from measured values, not from the nominal grade
Solution anneal and quench records demanded
ASTM A923 testing for intermetallic phase where specified
Impact testing where low-temperature service applies

grades.tell: Duplex fails on structure while the chemistry still reads clean

grades.name: Inconel 600
grades.summary: The original nickel-chromium-iron alloy for heat and corrosion resistance, still specified widely for furnace and chemical service.
service: Oxidising and carburising atmospheres to roughly 1100 °C
Resists chloride stress-corrosion cracking
Heat treatment fixtures, furnace components, chemical processing

verify.risk: Nickel at 72 % minimum makes 600 an expensive alloy to make honestly, and the pressure is always on the nickel floor. Iron drifting above the 10 % ceiling is the usual sign that the melt was stretched.
regime: PMI reading nickel against the 72 % minimum
Iron verified against the 6.0–10.0 % window
Certificate matched to the delivered heat

grades.tell: A 72 % nickel floor is expensive to hold honestly

grades.name: Inconel 601
grades.summary: An aluminium-bearing development of 600 that forms a tenacious oxide skin, giving markedly better high-temperature oxidation resistance.
service: Cyclic high-temperature oxidation to roughly 1200 °C
Furnace muffles and retorts, radiant tubes, thermal processing
Aluminium addition drives the oxidation resistance

verify.risk: Aluminium is the entire reason to buy 601 over 600. A heat below the 1.0 % floor is functionally 600 sold at a premium, and it will scale in exactly the cyclic service it was chosen for.
regime: PMI reading aluminium against the 1.0–1.7 % window
Chromium verified against the 21.0–25.0 % window
Certificate matched to the delivered heat

grades.tell: Without its aluminium, 601 is 600 at a premium

grades.name: Inconel X-750
grades.summary: A precipitation-hardening variant of 600, using titanium and aluminium to deliver high strength and relaxation resistance at temperature.
service: Springs, fasteners and rotor components to roughly 700 °C
Excellent relaxation resistance under sustained load
Properties depend on a controlled ageing cycle

mechanical.value: Age hardened, ASTM B637 — condition to be specified on order

verify.risk: Like 718, X-750 is a heat-treatment grade. Chemistry inside limits proves nothing about whether the ageing cycle was run correctly, and an under-aged spring relaxes in service.
regime: Heat treatment records demanded and read
Hardness verification on the delivered heat
PMI for Ti and Al against B637

grades.tell: An under-aged spring relaxes in service and tests fine cold

grades.name: Incoloy 800
grades.summary: The base nickel-iron-chromium grade of the 800 family, used where oxidation and carburisation resistance matter more than creep strength.
service: Process piping and heat exchangers to roughly 600 °C
Resists oxidation, carburisation and chloride stress-corrosion cracking
Where sustained creep service is required, specify 800H or 800HT

verify.risk: The risk on 800 runs the other way to 800H: buyers are sometimes sold 800 against an 800H requirement. If the application involves sustained high temperature, the grade designation on the order is the thing to check first.
regime: Confirmation that 800, not 800H, is what the application actually requires
PMI for Ni and Cr against B409
Certificate matched to the delivered heat

grades.tell: The risk runs backwards: 800 sold against an 800H requirement

grades.name: Incoloy 925
grades.summary: An age-hardenable development of 825, adding titanium and aluminium to reach high strength while keeping the corrosion resistance of the base alloy.
service: Sour gas wellhead and downhole components
High strength with resistance to sulphide stress cracking
Often specified to NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156

mechanical.value: Solution treated & aged — condition to be specified on order

verify.risk: 925 is usually bought for sour service, where the qualifying document is the NACE compliance record and the hardness result, not the chemistry. Material supplied without hardness verification cannot be shown to meet MR0175 whatever the certificate says.
regime: Hardness verification against the NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156 limit
Heat treatment records demanded
PMI for Ti and Mo against B805

grades.tell: Bought for sour service, qualified by hardness, not chemistry

grades.name: Monel K-500
grades.summary: Age-hardenable Monel, using aluminium and titanium to roughly triple the yield strength of 400 while keeping its seawater performance.
service: Pump shafts, propeller shafts, fasteners and valve stems in marine service
Strength of a structural alloy with the corrosion behaviour of Monel 400
Non-magnetic and spark-resistant

mechanical.value: Age hardened — condition to be specified on order

verify.risk: K-500 is vulnerable to hydrogen embrittlement if over-aged or over-hardened, which makes the heat treatment record and the hardness result the safety-critical documents. Aluminium below the 2.30 % floor means the age hardening cannot reach specified strength.
regime: Hardness verification on the delivered material
Heat treatment records demanded and read
PMI for Al and Ti against B865

grades.tell: Over-ageing buys strength and hydrogen embrittlement together

grades.name: Hastelloy B-2
grades.summary: A nickel-molybdenum alloy built for hydrochloric acid and other strongly reducing conditions, with chromium deliberately kept low.
service: Hydrochloric acid at all concentrations and temperatures
Sulphuric, acetic and phosphoric acid in reducing conditions
Not for oxidising service or ferric and cupric contamination

verify.risk: B-2 is prone to intermetallic precipitation in the heat-affected zone, so as-welded performance depends entirely on the solution anneal being right. Iron or chromium above the ceilings compromises the reducing-acid resistance the alloy exists for.
regime: PMI reading Mo against the 26.0–30.0 % window
Iron and chromium verified against their maximums
Solution anneal records demanded
Corrosion testing where the service is severe

grades.tell: The weld zone is where B-2 gives way, not the plate

grades.name: Hastelloy B-3
grades.summary: A modernised B-family alloy with markedly better thermal stability than B-2, resisting the intermetallic precipitation that limits the older grade.
service: Hydrochloric acid and reducing service where B-2 fabrication risk is unacceptable
Far more tolerant of welding and thermal cycling than B-2
Still not for oxidising conditions

verify.risk: B-3 and B-2 both quote as "Hastelloy B", which is all it takes for the two to be interchanged. They are not equivalent: B-3's chromium and iron windows are what give it thermal stability, and B-2 supplied against a B-3 specification will crack where B-3 would not.
regime: PMI distinguishing the Cr 1.0–3.0 % and Fe 1.0–3.0 % windows from B-2
Carbon verified against the 0.01 % maximum
Written confirmation of the UNS number before the PO

grades.tell: B-2 and B-3 both quote as "Hastelloy B" and are not equivalent

grades.name: Hastelloy X
grades.summary: A nickel-chromium-iron-molybdenum alloy combining oxidation resistance with high-temperature strength and exceptional fabricability.
service: Gas turbine combustion components, ducting and burner cans
Oxidation resistance to roughly 1200 °C
Good strength retention under sustained high temperature

verify.risk: Carbon on Hastelloy X sits in a band rather than under a ceiling, because the alloy needs it for high-temperature strength. A heat below 0.05 % will not perform at temperature even though a chemistry check against a maximum would pass it.
regime: Carbon verified against the 0.05–0.15 % band, not a maximum
PMI for Cr, Mo and Fe against B435
Solution anneal records demanded

grades.tell: Carbon sits in a band, so a chemistry check against a maximum passes it

grades.name: 904L
grades.summary: A high-alloy austenitic stainless with copper added for sulphuric acid resistance, sitting between standard stainless and the nickel alloys in both performance and price.
service: Sulphuric and phosphoric acid service
Good resistance to chloride pitting and stress-corrosion cracking
Low carbon gives good as-welded performance

verify.risk: 904L is the natural substitute to offer against an Incoloy 825 order, and nickel is most of what it costs, so nickel is where the dilution pressure sits. Copper below the 1.0 % floor removes the sulphuric acid resistance that is the reason to choose it.
regime: PMI reading nickel against the 23.0–28.0 % window
Copper verified against the 1.0–2.0 % window
Carbon verified against the 0.020 % maximum
Confirmation the order is 904L and not a substituted 825 requirement

grades.tell: Diluted on nickel, because nickel is most of what it costs

grades.name: Duplex 2205
grades.summary: The workhorse duplex stainless: roughly twice the yield strength of 316L with far better chloride stress-corrosion cracking resistance, at a lower nickel cost.
service: Process piping, pressure vessels and tanks in chloride service
Marine, desalination, oil and gas gathering systems
PREN typically 34 or above

verify.risk: The older S31803 designation has wider composition windows than S32205 and is still supplied against 2205 orders. As with all duplex, the real risk is structural: a bad anneal leaves sigma phase and a ferrite balance out of range while the chemistry certificate reads perfectly.
regime: Confirmation of S32205 rather than the wider S31803 windows
Ferrite content measured on the delivered material
PREN calculated from measured values
ASTM A923 testing for intermetallic phase where specified

grades.tell: The wider S31803 windows still ship against 2205 orders
